title: Smart Objects in Photoshop - Day 16
summary: PHLEARN's Day 16 in the 30 Days of Photoshop series explores smart objects and their non-destructive workflow. The tutorial demonstrates how smart objects preserve resolution when scaling, how they differ from rasterized layers, and how they can be edited by opening their contents as a nested document. Aaron Nace walks through building a boxed advertisement: importing images as smart objects, resizing non-destructively, applying non-destructive filters like Gaussian blur, and using masking and dynamic text to composite foreground and background. The video also covers saving the work as a PSD to preserve layers, relinking or replacing smart object contents to update assets, and advanced techniques such as extracting and overlaying reflections with clipping masks and levels for a more realistic result. Throughout, the emphasis is on iterative editing, updating linked assets, and the practical advantages of smart objects in complex composites, with notes on trade-offs like increased file size.

sections.title: Introduction to smart objects and setup
sections.description: Aaron introduces smart objects and outlines the goal to build a boxed advertisement, comparing a smart object with a non-smart object to show the impact on image resolution when scaling.

sections.title: Smart vs. non-smart scaling demonstration
sections.description: Importing a second JPEG, duplicating and rasterizing the non-smart layer to illustrate how scaling affects information versus a smart object that preserves data.

sections.title: Non-destructive vs baked blur on smart vs non-smart
sections.description: Applying Gaussian blur to both objects; demonstrates that blur on a smart object remains adjustable while blur on a rasterized layer is baked into pixels.

sections.title: Smart object-based composition and masking
sections.description: Demonstrates deleting a background, masking the smart object into an advertisement, and using a dynamic text element with masking to blend foreground and background.

sections.title: Saving, PSD workflow, and relinking contents
sections.description: Discusses when to save as PSD versus JPEG, how to relink or replace the smart object contents, and how linked PSDs enable updating assets while preserving edits.

sections.title: Updating linked smart objects and reflection extraction
sections.description: Shows updating a smart object by relinking, clipping a reflected texture to the ad, converting to a smart object for a levels adjustment, and using screen blend to reveal subtle reflections for realism.

sections.title: Conclusion and benefits of smart objects
sections.description: Recap of smart object benefits (resizing, non-destructive filters, updating linked content) and a note on the trade-off of slightly larger file sizes.
